questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(11, 16.5, 22)

(14.5, 20, 25.5)

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent

digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1

and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (2nd number × 2) - 1st number = 3rd number.

Now,

For, 11, 16.5, 22

⇒ (16.5 × 2) - 11

= 33 - 11 = 22.

For, 14.5, 20, 25.5

⇒ (20 × 2) - 14.5 

= 40 - 14.5 = 25.5.

Similarly, for:** 18, 23.5, 29**

**⇒ (23.5 × 2) - 18 **

**= 47 - 18 = 29.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All cards are postcards.

Some postcards are books.

All books are novels.

Conclusions:

I. Some postcards are novels.

II. No card is a book.

III. All cards are novels.

options.text: Only II and III conclusion follow
Only I and II conclusion follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59bea7b57b59b81da7cbfcce03f2c20df4fbd873dffe10d44b76c70477606942.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some postcards are novels → Follow (As some postcards are books and all books are novels. As some part of the postcards is common with books which whole comes in novels, therefore it is false.)

II. No card is a book → Does not follow (As all cards are postcards and some postcards are books. As no direct relation is given between cards and books, therefore it is false.)

III. All cards are novels → Does not follow (As all cards are postcards, some postcards are books and all books are novels. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion I follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
